messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High latency spike detected for runtime service 'inference-gateway' in us-west-2. latency p95 > 1200ms, error-rate increased by 8% — triggered paging policy.

devon (oncall): saw it, jumping in. pinging runtime and sre.

maria (runtime): ack. I'm looking at canary rollout 2026-03-15T02:10Z (continous-batching-v2). Metrics show per-request queue time rising and a lot of kernel fallback events.

kevin (sre): for context, NODES: pool-usw2-gpu-3 showing steady increase in paged kernel fallbacks -> lots of NVME reads. Could be KV cache thrash after the new batching behavior.

jordan (customer-ops): any known customer impact? any large customers on reserved capacity hitting errors?

devon (oncall): alerting accounts with high p99 latency. So far two customers (AcmeCo, Dataly) reported slow responses in dashboards. No 5xx spikes yet.

maria (runtime): quick analysis: continuous-batching-v2 increases batch eviction window to 2s and reorders KV cache lifetime. If workload has many short sequences, we get cache churn -> fallback to kernel path. That explains the disk reads and latency.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout 2026-03-15T02:10Z to 10% complete for service inference-gateway. Flag continuous-batching-v2 enabled.

kevin (sre): suggestion: stop traffic to the canary and flip the killflag for continuous-batching-v2 (roll back feature flag) while we evaluate. This is low-risk and reversible.

maria (runtime): agree. Rolling through console now:
```
# Disable flag for canary group
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/flags/continuous-batching-v2/disable \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 
```
Keep an eye on the canary nodes (pool-usw2-canary-*) for kernel fallback counts.

devon (oncall): doing the disable. Leaving 5% canary for diagnostics only.

ops-bot: action-log: feature flag continuous-batching-v2 disabled for canary (user devon). timestamp 1987654350.

maria (runtime): metrics after disable: p95 down from 1250ms -> 430ms in canary cluster, kernel fallback events drop ~90%. Looks promising.

kevin (sre): nice. Next step: cut traffic back to baseline model variant for affected clients while we validate. Jordan, can you coordinate with AcmeCo/Dataly and offer a short status/mitigation note?

jordan (customer-ops): on it. Messaging them now: "We're aware of increased latency; rollback in progress to previous behavior. No data lost; ETA 15-30 min to stabilize." Will update if they escalate.

maria (runtime): root cause hypothesis: KV cache policy in v2 was too aggressive for workloads with many short prompts -> cache churn -> page-in storm -> kernel fallback -> batch queue delay -> latency SLO breach. Also found a regression in the eviction handshake that caused slightly higher-than-expected cache miss rates.

kevin (sre): we'll run a controlled rollback for the rest of the rollout. Plan: 1) keep canary disabled 2) abort canary expansion 3) flip global killflag / revert rollout 4) monitor for 30m then confirm. Any objections?

maria (runtime): no objections. I'll prepare a hotfix branch with adjusted eviction windows and a unit test to reproduce short-sequence traffic. But do not deploy new behavior until next release.

devon (oncall): initiating global rollback via controlplane, aborting current deployment.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout abort requested by devon. Rollout ID r-2026-03-15T02:10 aborted. timestamp 1987654482.

ops-bot: traffic-router: redirecting canary traffic back to stable model variant m-stable-20260301 for affected routes.

maria (runtime): monitoring: p95 across us-west-2 back to ~420-480ms cluster-wide, error-rates normalized. Kernel fallback counters trending to baseline.

jordan (customer-ops): updated AcmeCo and Dataly: they acknowledged, one asked for postmortem. I'll collect any logs they want.

kevin (sre): escalations? None active. Creating incident ticket INC-19876 for postmortem and tracking rollback + fix. Assigning to Maria and Kevin.

devon (oncall): handing off to night oncall, sam (oncall). Sam, please confirm the cluster remains stable and close the incident when green for 60m.

sam (oncall): acked (via DM). Will watch.

maria (runtime): quick note for postmortem: reproduce locally with high qps of short-sequence prompts + continuous-batching-v2 enabled; add integration test to CI that simulates KV churn. Also add an alert for kernel-fallback rate per node to catch earlier.

kevin (sre): adding alert: kernel_fallback_rate > 5/min per node for 5m -> page to oncall + paging escalation.

devon (oncall): incident summary: deployment rollout of continuous-batching-v2 caused KV cache eviction churn on short-seq workloads -> kernel fallback and elevated p95 latency. Rapid mitigation: disabled feature flag for canary, aborted rollout, redirected canary traffic to stable variant. Impact: elevated latency for some customers (AcmeCo, Dataly) for ~18m, no data loss. Owners: Maria (runtime), Kevin (SRE). Incident ticket INC-19876 created. Postmortem POC: maria.

ops-bot: incident-bot: Incident INC-19876 created. Severity S2.

sam (oncall): watching metrics now. Will ping channel if anything changes.

devon (oncall): thanks all. Follow-up items: 1) patch eviction handshake + test, 2) add kernel-fallback alert, 3) improve canary gating criteria for cache-heavy changes. We'll draft a postmortem template and link it here. :memo:

jordan (customer-ops): copying AcmeCo support thread to incident ticket for visibility.

maria (runtime): I'm going to sketch the fix and a safe rollout playbook. Will attach to INC-19876.

sam (oncall): no new alerts in the last 10m, closing watch in 50m if stable.

devon (oncall): closing channel for active ops. Leave comments on INC-19876. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
